headline: The agent is expected to trust the customer's claim that the disputes were approved and then write corrected reward values, but it has no way to check dispute status, the same conversation in task_027 expects the opposite, and one gold value (1500) contradicts the KB's round-down rule (1499).

issues.summary: Whether to apply reward corrections depends on cash_back_disputes.status (RESOLVED in task_026 via auto_resolve_disputes=True, SUBMITTED in task_027), but no agent tool reads that table, and dispute-tool results go only to the user simulator. Tasks 026 and 027 use the same user, transactions, and dispute set, and their Phase-2 user messages are word-for-word identical, so the agent sees the same conversation in both.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004: "Look up the user's resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database to find the transaction_id values that need rewards adjustments."

tools.py get_user_dispute_history_7291 docstring: "Retrieve a user's credit card transaction dispute history from the transaction_disputes table" (not cash_back_disputes); no other KnowledgeTools method queries cash_back_disputes
orchestrator.py Orchestrator.step: ENV tool results for a USER tool call are routed back to the user (to_role = from_role), never to the agent

task_026 Phase 2 and task_027 Phase 2 user line: "Great, I've submitted all the disputes. I just got a notification that they've all been approved and resolved! Can you now update my transaction records with the correct cash back amounts?"
task_026.initial_state: auto_resolve_disputes = true; task_027.initial_state: auto_resolve_disputes = false
issues.why_it_matters: Replays confirm that refusing the updates fails task_026 and applying them fails task_027. Because the agent's observations are the same in both tasks, any single policy (trust the customer, or refuse without verification) passes at most one of them. Each task's outcome reflects the agent's disposition, not its use of evidence.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an agent read tool for cash_back_disputes (e.g. get_cash_back_disputes_by_user, documented in doc_..._(general)_004) so the agent can verify RESOLVED vs SUBMITTED, and add that read to both golds so it is logged and required.

issues.summary: gold[10] writes '1500 points' for Zoom $149.99 on Business Silver at 10% = 1499.9 points. The KB rounding policy floors this to 1499, and doc_..._(general)_004 tells the agent to write the correct whole-number value.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004: "new_rewards_earned: a string formatted as 'X points' where X is the correct whole-number point value"
db.json txn_a8f1c2d3e411: Zoom Video, Software, '$149.99', 09/15/2025 (after the 08/13/2025 promo end)
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that follows the documented rule writes '1499 points'. A replay of gold with that one value changed gives a different agent hash (cab5086583a3...), so policy-faithful work fails. Only an agent that misses the rounding doc and rounds half-up matches.
issues.suggested_fix: Change gold[10] to '1499 points' (and re-seed task_020/026/027 non-error rows to floor), or change the KB rounding policy to round-half-up.

issues.summary: The dispute set is the same as task_020: seeded non-error rewards follow round-half-up, while the KB prescribes floor. Under the documented rule, nine transactions are over-credited by 1 point and are not in the gold.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
db.json txn_a8f1c2d3e402 Adobe $54.99 at 20% = 1099.8 -> floor 1099, stored '1100 points'
floor false positives: a8f1c2d3e402, a8f1c2d3e404, a8f1c2d3e406, a8f1c2d3e409, a8f1c2d3e414, b7e2d4c5f503, b7e2d4c5f507, b7e2d4c5f509, b7e2d4c5f512
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that applies the documented floor rule and treats over-credits as discrepancies has the user file 13 disputes instead of 4, which changes the hash.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-seed the nine non-error transactions with floor values.

solution_check: The Phase-1 dispute set under round-half-up is a8f1c2d3e403/b7e2d4c5f506/a8f1c2d3e410/a8f1c2d3e411, matching gold[2..5]. Corrected values: 315 x 20% = 6300, 255 x 4% = 1020, 380 x 10% = 3800, 149.99 x 10% = 1499.9 -> 1499 under the documented floor rule, where gold has 1500. The agent cannot confirm the disputes are RESOLVED, so applying the updates rests entirely on trusting the user.
prior_note: The prior review rated this Minor (rounding unwritten, natural rounding works). Under v1.0.1 grading the task is a Blocker: dispute status cannot be observed (indistinguishable from task_027), and the 1500 gold value contradicts the documented floor rule.
notes: The unlock (gold[6]) is in-memory only; update_transaction_rewards_3847 is a WRITE discoverable tool and is always logged to agent_discoverable_tools. JSON key order or spacing inside the inner arguments string does not change the hash (verified on the dispute calls), but ACTION grading is not used here (reward_basis = DB). Grading-model facts checked against the snapshot (tag v1.0.1, commit fc0055d): EnvironmentEvaluator replays gold on a fresh env and compares agent and user DB hashes exactly; _derive_read_log_allowlist collects agent_tool_name from gold call_discoverable_agent_tool actions and is passed whenever domain == banking_knowledge; call_discoverable_agent_tool and call_discoverable_user_tool parse with json.loads(parse_int=float); agent and user toolkits share one TransactionalDB; get_now() = 2025-11-14 03:40:00. All matched the prompt. Additional fact: user-tool outputs are returned only to the user simulator (Orchestrator.step routes ENV->USER), so the agent never sees dispute-tool status text. Replays were run with PYTHONPATH=snapshot/src via the repo venv (confirmed tau2.__file__ and DATA_DIR resolve to the snapshot).
